title: PRD: Cost Failure Isolator and Developer Guardrails
author: Anika Patel
body:
Title: PRD — Cost Failure Isolator and Developer Guardrails

Overview:
This PRD describes a cross-product feature (Optimize + Hosted API + Console) that introduces a defensive runtime and product surface to detect, isolate, and mitigate cost runaway events caused by developer mistakes, misconfigurations, experiments, or malicious inputs. The feature group is called the Cost Failure Isolator (CFI) and the Developer Guardrails UX. The goal is to protect customers and Redwood’s hosted capacity while preserving rapid developer iteration.

Why this exists:
- We see frequent cases where misconfigured loops, missing token limits, or large embedding requests generate unexpectedly high bills or saturated capacity for small teams.
- Current safety nets (quota, billing alerts) are reactive and slow; we need fast, deterministic isolation at the runtime and product surface.

Scope:
Included:
- Runtime-level automated short-circuiting and throttling for anomalous per-tenant consumption spikes.
- Per-route and per-API-key guardrails with developer-friendly defaults.
- Console UX and SDK warnings, local sandbox preflight checks, and optional canary policies.
- Audit logs and a rollback/fail-open policy for enterprise customers.

Excluded (non-goals):
- Replacing billing/chargeback systems.
- Deep behavioral filtering of model outputs (safety is handled elsewhere).

Goals (measurable):
1) Reduce incidence of tenant-level runaway events that require manual support intervention by 75% in the first 6 months.
2) Prevent > 90% of small-team billing spikes above 3x baseline without an explicit override.
3) Offer a non-intrusive developer experience: warnings in <200ms for SDK calls and a preflight sandbox with cost estimate within 1s.

Key user journeys:
1) Developer writes a loop calling text-generation in dev: SDK detects high token consumption pattern, warns locally, and requires an opt-in override to proceed beyond safe defaults.
2) A misconfigured integration in staging sends sudden high-volume embedding requests: runtime throttles to a soft-limit, queues suspicious requests for review, and surfaces action items in Console (pause key, revoke, or escalate).
3) Enterprise customer with strict SLAs wants transparent fail-open behavior during outages: CFI logs actions and notifies SRE but allows configurable fail-open.

Requirements (functional):
| ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | Per-API-key short-circuiting | API keys can be auto-paused when 1-minute token rate > X * baseline and X configurable | eng-platform/product |
| F-02 | Developer SDK preflight | SDK exposes preflightEstimate(request) that returns tokens, cost estimate, and risk score within 1s | eng-devex/product |
| F-03 | Console incident actions | Console shows active isolations, allows pause/whitelist/override with audit-entry | product/eng-platform |
| F-04 | Policy config API | Customers can set guardrail policies (soft-limit, hard-limit, notify-list) via API | product/eng-platform |

Requirements (non-functional):
- NF-01: Detection latency <= 5s from first anomalous request to throttling decision for hosted customers.
- NF-02: 99.9% of normal traffic must be unaffected (false-positive rate <0.1% over 30 days).
- NF-03: System telemetry must emit a standardized event for every isolation: {tenant, key, policy_id, action, reason, token_count}.

Runtime design (high level):
- Signal sources: per-API-key token counters, per-route counters, per-tenant baseline models (moving average and percentile), and session context.
- Decision engine: lightweight rule-evaluator with rate checks, burst-detection, simple ML anomaly detector (optional), and configurable policy layer. Decisions are signed and logged.
- Enforcement points: request ingress in serving runtime for hosted; local agent for Private builds that enforces customer policies against locally-provisioned quotas.

Behavioral policy primitives (config table):
| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| soft_limit_tokens_per_minute | integer | 50000 | Gradual soft throttle. SDK/Console warns when exceeded. |
| hard_limit_tokens_per_minute | integer | 250000 | Enforcement: automatic pause/queue when exceeded. |
| notify_emails | list | [] | Emails to notify on isolation event. |
| fail_open | boolean | false | If true, on control-plane failure, do not pause requests. Enterprise override. |
| sandbox_mode | enum | "estimate_only" | ["estimate_only","enforce_in_sandbox","allow_override"] |

SDK changes (developer experience):
- New API: preflightEstimate(request) -> {estimated_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, risk_level, suggested_limits}
- Runtime returns header: X-CFI-Action: none|warn|soft_throttle|paused and X-CFI-Policy-Id
- On warn or pause, SDK surfaces clear message with link to Console action page and CLI command.

Example SDK preflight response (JSON snippet):
{
  "estimated_tokens": "3120",
  "estimated_cost_usd": "0.0096",
  "risk_level": "medium",
  "suggested_limits": "reduce_max_tokens_to_512"
}

Console UX summary (key screens):
- Active Isolations: list with tenant, key, policy, tokens consumed, start time, action buttons (Pause Key, Whitelist, Revoke, Notify).
- Preflight Explorer: interactive sandbox to paste requests and get cost + risk.
- Policy Manager: create/edit guardrails, import defaults, per-environment presets.

Operational playbook (runbook excerpt):
1) Auto-isolation triggers: routing changes to soft_throttle for 30s and create incident in SRE queue.
2) If continued spike after 5 minutes, escalate to hard_pause and page oncall.
3) Customer-facing workflow: automated email + Console notification with steps to unpause or whitelist.

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Phase 0 (Q1 2026, internal beta): runtime metrics, basic soft/hard throttles, SDK preflight beta, internal tenants opt-in.
- Phase 1 (Q2 2026, developer beta): Console UX, public SDK release (warn-only), sandbox preflight.
- Phase 2 (Q3 2026, GA): full enforcement, policy API, audit logs, enterprise mode (fail-open/whitelist).

Metrics and evaluation:
- Primary metrics: number of manual interventions per month (target: -75%), median time-to-detect (target <10s), number of false-isolations (target <0.1% of transactions).
- Financial guardrails: track monthly tokens paused and measure impact on revenue/CS tickets.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Isolation decisions are policy metadata only; no PII needs to be logged.
- Audit logs must be retained according to tenant retention settings and available to enterprise auditors.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Default opt-in: all new API keys for non-enterprise customers will have CFI soft/warn enabled. Existing keys are opt-in during next SDK/Console prompt.
- Enterprise customers can request legacy behavior and a migration checklist is provided.

Testing plan:
- Synthetic runaway tests: simulated high token loops at variable rates to validate detection thresholds and false-positive rates.
- Chaos tests: inject delayed telemetry and control-plane partitions to verify fail-open/fail-closed behaviors.
- Developer UX tests: measure preflight latency on representative machines across regions.

Ownership and stakeholders:
- Product lead: Anika Patel (owner).
- Engineering: eng-platform (enforcement), eng-serving-runtime (ingress hooks), eng-devex (SDKs), eng-sre (monitoring/runbooks).
- Security/Compliance: review audit retention and enterprise fail-open policy.

Open questions and decisions:
1) Baseline calculation method: moving-average vs percentile baseline — decision: start with 10-minute exponential moving average, revisit after 3 months.
2) Default thresholds tuning — decision: expose conservative defaults and allow customer override via Policy API.
3) Anomaly detector inclusion — optional ML detector to be piloted in Phase 1.

Appendix: Sample policy creation CLI:
# create a policy that soft-throttles at 60k tokens/min and hard-pauses at 300k
redwood policies create --name "dev-guard" \
  --soft_limit_tokens_per_minute=60000 \
  --hard_limit_tokens_per_minute=300000 \
  --notify_emails=devops@acme.example \
  --sandbox_mode=estimate_only
